newsitem.title: UK: UK company annual reports fall short -- survey.
newsitem.headline: UK company annual reports fall short -- survey.

text.p: British public companies are not providing shareholders with the best information in their annual reports, according to a survey released on Monday.

Arthur Andersen, the accountancy and consulting firm, said its survey of 100, randomly-selected company annual reports found that fewer than 20 percent of the smaller, listed companies have clearly adopted the recommendations of the 1993 ASB Statement on Operating and Financial Reviews.
Eighty percent of the Top 350 companies have clearly adopted the recommendations.

However, of the 46 percent of the surveyed companies which have adopted the recommendations, Arthur Andersen said the survey found a considerable overlap between the accounts and the narrative sections and a paucity of forward-looking information.

"The best annual reports are notable for the quality of information not the quantity of financial data included," Philip Randall, managing partner for Arthur Andersen's UK Audit and Business Advisory, said in a statement.

More than 80 percent of the surveyed companies which provided Operating and Financial Reviews gave no clear identification of significant risks and uncertainties in the company's main business lines in their annual reports.
More than 50 percent gave no clue to future investment plans, the survey found.
